paragraphs: The Orienteering Problem with Time Windows asks how to collect the greatest total score by visiting selected locations while respecting when each location can be visited. Choosing more valuable stops can conflict with travel and scheduling constraints. The paper studies an exact solution method, so its aim is to accelerate the search while retaining the ability to find an optimal solution.

The authors combine dynamic programming with a learned choice of relaxation: a way of loosening problem restrictions within the algorithm. A graph convolutional network predicts directed edges that define this relaxation. It learns from optimal solutions supplied as supervised training labels. Learning therefore influences how the exact algorithm organizes its work, rather than simply producing a route that replaces exact optimization.

Experiments report a 38% speedup over the leading exact algorithm on Solomon’s benchmark and more than a sevenfold improvement on the harder Cordeau’s benchmark. These results show that learned guidance can improve an exact solver substantially on the evaluated problems, connecting data-driven predictions with established optimization machinery.
neurips-2025-a-learning-augmented-dynami.tldr: A learned graph model chooses relaxations that accelerate exact dynamic programming for route planning with time windows.

paragraphs: An animated QR code has two jobs: it should look appealing as moving imagery, and it should preserve the visual structure needed for decoding. These goals can compete as appearance changes over time. AnimateQR introduces a generative framework that manages this balance during the creation of animated codes, extending beyond the static QR images addressed by earlier methods.

The framework controls brightness at several spatial scales. This hierarchical luminance guidance helps maintain decodable patterns while leaving room for artistic variation. A second mechanism progressively adjusts guidance over both space and time throughout diffusion denoising. Together, the controls influence how the animation develops, with the aim of coordinating visual quality and scan reliability rather than optimizing either in isolation.

The reported experiments achieve a 96% decoding success rate, compared with 56% for the baseline. Visual preference scores also improve, from 2.3 to 7.2 on a ten-point scale. These findings support the framework’s ability to improve both objectives in the evaluated settings; the reported decoding rate does not amount to universal scanning success.
neurips-2025-animateqr-bridging-aestheti.tldr: AnimateQR coordinates brightness and motion guidance to generate animated QR codes with improved visual appeal and decoding success.

paragraphs: Normalizing flows generate data through transformations that can be reversed, allowing both sampling and likelihood calculation. Their linear layers must be expressive while keeping inversion and determinant calculations affordable. CDFlow addresses this design problem by replacing a general dense matrix with a product of circulant and diagonal matrices.

For input dimension n, the construction uses m diagonal matrices and m−1 circulant matrices. It reduces parameter complexity from O(n²) to O(mn), while supporting approximation of arbitrary linear transformations. Using the Fast Fourier Transform, inversion takes O(mn log n) time and log-determinant calculation takes O(mn), compared with O(n³) for the general dense calculations described in the abstract. The costs therefore depend on both input size and the number of factors.

The authors build a complete flow model around these layers and report strong density estimation on natural images, alongside effective modeling of periodic data. At 96 channels, inverse and log-determinant computations are respectively 1.17 and 4.31 times faster than with a general dense matrix. These measurements concern those operations at that channel count.
neurips-2025-cdflow-building-invertible-.tldr: CDFlow uses structured matrix products to make invertible generative layers more economical in parameters and computation.

paragraphs: Asking several language models to label the same item can reduce the influence of an individual model’s biases. However, collecting every model’s answer for every item makes annotation expensive. Cost-aware Majority Voting, or CaMVo, selects a subset of models for each incoming example, aiming to retain reliable labels while spending less on queries.

The selection depends on contextual embeddings that represent the item being labeled. A LinUCB-based mechanism chooses models, while a Bayesian estimator uses confidence scores to estimate a lower bound on each model’s labeling accuracy. The selected answers are combined through weighted voting. This allows the system to make different querying decisions for different examples without requiring pretraining or ground-truth labels for the framework.

On MMLU and IMDB Movie Review data, CaMVo achieves accuracy comparable to or better than querying all models and taking a majority vote, while substantially reducing labeling costs. The findings support adaptive model selection as a practical way to manage annotation expense in the evaluated settings, rather than assuming that every item needs the same collection of model opinions.
neurips-2025-cost-aware-llm-based-online.tldr: CaMVo adaptively chooses which language models to query for each label, reducing annotation costs while maintaining or improving accuracy in its evaluations.

paragraphs: Virtual staining changes the appearance of tissue images to resemble another dye or staining style. A central difficulty is separating the tissue’s pathology from the requested color tone. When these conditions become entangled, normal regions can receive staining associated with disease, or diseased regions can receive inappropriate staining. The paper calls this error pathology leakage.

D-VST uses separate pathology and tone encoders, together with a two-stage training curriculum, to disentangle those conditions. This design aims to allow tone adjustments while eliminating pathology leakage. To process whole-slide images containing billions of pixels, the framework also introduces frequency-aware adaptive patch sampling. That component supports efficient, high-quality inference at ultra-high resolution in a zero-shot setting.

Experiments cover three virtual staining tasks involving four dyes. The authors report better image quality and pathological accuracy than existing generative adversarial network and diffusion methods. The contribution connects two requirements of whole-slide virtual staining: preserving pathology during appearance changes and making inference manageable at very large image sizes. The stated results concern generated staining images and their evaluated accuracy.
neurips-2025-d-vst-diffusion-transformer.tldr: D-VST separates pathology from color tone and adapts patch sampling to produce controllable virtual staining of whole-slide tissue images.

paragraphs: A useful visual taxonomy should organize broad categories and finer distinctions together. Existing deep hierarchical clustering methods often tie their structure to a known number of classes and make limited use of the representative clusters found between the top and bottom of the hierarchy. This paper learns those intermediate prototypes directly from unlabeled data.

Deep taxonomic networks use a latent-variable model with a complete binary tree of Gaussian mixture components as its prior. Variational inference fits this large hierarchy without assuming the true label counts. The authors analytically show that optimizing the evidence lower bound, the model’s training objective, encourages hierarchical relationships among prototypes. Thus, the hierarchy is part of the learned representation rather than merely a final arrangement of flat clusters.

Across diverse image classification datasets, the method outperforms baselines under an evaluation mechanism that uses prototype clusters from every hierarchical level. Qualitative results show interpretable groupings spanning coarse semantic categories and fine visual distinctions. Together, these findings support evaluating and learning the information held throughout a taxonomy, including its intermediate levels.
neurips-2025-deep-taxonomic-networks-for.tldr: Deep taxonomic networks discover interpretable hierarchies of visual prototypes from unlabeled data without assuming the true number of classes.

paragraphs: Object binding means bringing together features that belong to the same object. The paper asks whether pretrained vision transformers acquire this ability without an explicitly imposed object-centered attention mechanism. Its central test is whether patch representations encode IsSameObject: whether two image patches belong to one object.

A similarity probe decodes this relationship from embeddings across transformer layers with over 90% accuracy. The signal emerges reliably in the studied DINO, MAE, and CLIP models, but is markedly weaker in ImageNet-supervised models. This difference suggests that the ability depends on pretraining objectives rather than following automatically from the transformer architecture. The authors also locate the relationship in a low-dimensional subspace alongside object features.

The study goes beyond showing that the signal can be read out: it finds that the signal guides attention. Removing it from activations degrades downstream performance and works against the learning objective. These observations support the interpretation that object binding contributes to the studied models’ computations, challenging the view that vision transformers lack such an ability.
neurips-2025-does-object-binding-natural.tldr: The studied vision transformers encode and use information about which patches belong to the same object, with strength depending on pretraining.

paragraphs: Text-to-speech systems must do more than pronounce ordinary sentences clearly. They also need to convey emotion, handle questions, and interpret difficult written forms. EmergentTTS-Eval targets these demands through six scenarios: emotions, paralinguistic expression, foreign words, syntactic complexity, difficult pronunciation such as URLs and formulas, and questions.

The benchmark automates both the creation of test cases and their assessment. Starting with a small set of human-written seed prompts, language models iteratively produce examples targeting structural, phonetic, and prosodic challenges. This yields 1,645 samples. A large audio language model then judges generated speech along dimensions including emotion, prosody, intonation, and pronunciation, making the framework extensible beyond its initial examples.

The authors evaluate open-source and proprietary speech systems and report that the benchmark reveals detailed differences in their abilities. Automated judgments show high correlation with human preferences and provide robust assessment in the reported evaluation. The contribution is a scalable method for testing nuanced speech behavior, with both code and data released, rather than a single overall measure of speech quality.
neurips-2025-emergenttts-eval-evaluating.tldr: EmergentTTS-Eval combines generated challenge prompts with an audio-model judge to assess nuanced text-to-speech performance.

paragraphs: Strong performance in mathematics and coding does not automatically translate into success on puzzles requiring no specialist knowledge. ENIGMATA addresses this gap with 36 puzzle tasks across seven categories. Each task includes a generator capable of producing unlimited examples at controlled difficulty and a rule-based verifier that can automatically check solutions.

This pairing supplies both training problems and verifiable rewards for reinforcement learning. The authors also introduce ENIGMATA-Eval and develop strategies for training across multiple tasks. Controlling difficulty and checking answers programmatically makes the suite useful for scaling training and examining which forms of puzzle reasoning improve.

The resulting Qwen2.5-32B-ENIGMATA model consistently surpasses o3-mini-high and o1 on the reported puzzle benchmarks, scoring 32.8% on ARC-AGI and 0.6% on ARC-AGI 2. The authors report transfer to other puzzle benchmarks and mathematical reasoning with little multitask trade-off. Adding ENIGMATA puzzle data to the larger Seed1.5-Thinking model also improves advanced mathematics and STEM results. These findings support benefits beyond the training puzzles while showing that performance still varies considerably across benchmarks.
neurips-2025-enigmata-scaling-logical-re.tldr: ENIGMATA supplies controllable puzzles and automatic verifiers for reinforcement learning that improves puzzle reasoning and transfers to other reasoning tasks.

paragraphs: A coding model can exploit familiar wording and code patterns without reliably following a program’s formal meaning. TF-Bench evaluates this distinction through type inference in System F. The task places reasoning within a formal deductive framework, providing a program-centered basis for checking answers rather than relying on associations between natural language and code.

The authors also construct TF-Bench_pure using verified transformations that remove natural language irrelevant to program semantics. This variant is designed to keep the reasoning task focused on the program’s semantic content. Comparing performance in such a setting helps examine capabilities that might otherwise be obscured by helpful surface cues in conventional coding benchmarks.

The best-performing model in the reported evaluation, Claude-3.7-sonnet, reaches 55.85% accuracy on TF-Bench_pure. The authors additionally propose two metrics for the robustness and effectiveness of extended reasoning. Their findings identify substantial weaknesses on this formal reasoning task and provide a more targeted way to study whether additional reasoning effort produces dependable semantic understanding.
neurips-2025-evaluating-program-semantic.tldr: TF-Bench uses formal type inference to test program-semantics reasoning and reveals substantial weaknesses in the evaluated language models.

paragraphs: Image-to-video generation becomes more demanding when a scene’s cast must change during the clip. This paper focuses on Frame In and Frame Out: making an object leave the visible scene or introducing a new subject using an identity reference. Users specify a motion trajectory to guide these entrances and exits.

The task connects several difficult requirements. The movement must follow the requested path, the subject’s identity must remain recognizable, and the video must remain coherent over time while synthesizing detail. The authors introduce an efficient video Diffusion Transformer designed for identity preservation and motion control. Its purpose is to support these changes in scene contents within an image-to-video generation framework.

The contribution also includes a semi-automatically curated dataset and an evaluation protocol tailored to the task. The reported evaluation finds that the proposed approach significantly outperforms existing baselines. Together, these components make entrances and exits a concrete generation problem with dedicated training material, a model architecture, and a way to assess performance, rather than treating them only as incidental motion.
neurips-2025-frame-in-n-out-unbounded-co.tldr: Frame In-N-Out enables trajectory-controlled entrances and exits in image-to-video generation while preserving subject identity.

paragraphs: Attention works across many kinds of data, but incorporating several scales and modalities into one mechanism is less straightforward. The paper argues that existing hierarchical adaptations often rely on heuristics tied to particular structures. It instead starts by defining a mathematical representation for data with multiple modalities and scales.

From that representation, the authors derive attention through entropy minimization. The resulting formulation incorporates biases from the problem’s hierarchy and geometry while staying as close as possible to standard softmax attention in the specified mathematical sense. This is the stated meaning of optimality: proximity to ordinary attention while accommodating structural information, rather than a claim of universally best task performance.

A dynamic programming algorithm computes the derived mechanism efficiently. The authors show two uses within transformers: training models from scratch for hierarchical or multimodal settings, and adding hierarchical information to conventional pretrained models after training. The latter produces more efficient models in a zero-shot manner. The work therefore offers a shared mathematical foundation and a computational method for bringing structured relationships into attention.
neurips-2025-hierarchical-self-attention.tldr: The paper derives hierarchical attention from entropy minimization and computes it efficiently for both newly trained and pretrained transformers.

paragraphs: Subject-driven generation should preserve a subject’s visual characteristics, but broad semantic similarity can overlook appearance inconsistencies. This paper separates visual and semantic features within pretrained diffusion backbones so that corresponding image regions can be compared in both ways. The motivation is that a model capable of synthesizing images must contain visual information alongside its well-known semantic features.

Because suitable annotated correspondences are lacking, the authors build an automated pipeline that creates paired images with semantic and visual correspondence annotations from existing subject-driven generation datasets. A contrastive architecture uses these pairs to disentangle the two feature types. The resulting representations support a metric called Visual Semantic Matching, or VSM, for measuring visual inconsistencies.

Empirical results show that VSM quantifies these inconsistencies better than global feature metrics based on CLIP, DINO, and vision-language models. It can also locate inconsistent regions within an image. That combination makes the assessment more informative: it measures the problem and identifies where it occurs, providing localized feedback about preservation of a generated subject’s appearance.
neurips-2025-mind-the-glitch-visual-corr.tldr: Mind-the-Glitch separates visual and semantic diffusion features to measure and localize appearance inconsistencies in subject-driven generation.

paragraphs: Standard transformer attention becomes expensive as sequence length grows because its computation scales quadratically. MonarchAttention approximates softmax attention using Monarch matrices, a structured matrix family. The goal is an approximation that transfers to existing transformers without additional training and runs efficiently on modern GPU hardware.

The method uses the variational form of softmax to construct an optimization algorithm for an approximate projection onto Monarch matrices. For sequence length N and dimension d, its computation scales as Θ(N√N d), with Θ(Nd) memory and input/output complexity. Optimized kernels use high-throughput tensor cores, connecting the mathematical reduction in work to the hardware that executes it.

The authors report minimal performance loss without additional training, including when replacing every attention layer. Against FlashAttention-2, measured wall-time speedups are 1.4 times at sequence length 256, 4.5 times at 4K, and 8.2 times at 16K. Evaluations span vision and language tasks and multiple architectures. These results support the approach’s combination of practical acceleration and accurate approximation across the tested contexts.
neurips-2025-monarchattention-zero-shot-.tldr: MonarchAttention replaces softmax attention with a hardware-efficient structured approximation that accelerates tested transformers without additional training.

paragraphs: Selective prediction gives a forecaster freedom to choose the time window covered by a forecast. Earlier results show that this flexibility can support nontrivial prediction accuracy for many statistics without distributional assumptions or expert advice. However, those results depend on the ability to begin predicting at any time. This paper examines what happens when that freedom is restricted.

The proposed Prediction with Limited Selectivity model allows prediction to start only at designated times within the overall horizon. The authors study the best achievable error for individual instances as well as through an average-case analysis. This separates the effect of a particular pattern of available start times from behavior across randomly generated instances.

The main tool is a complexity measure that yields instance-dependent bounds on optimal prediction error. For randomly generated instances, the bounds match with high probability. That qualified matching result gives a tight characterization in the stated random setting. More broadly, the work makes the availability of prediction opportunities an explicit part of understanding how accurate a selective forecaster can be.
neurips-2025-online-prediction-with-limi.tldr: The paper characterizes prediction error when forecasters can start only at selected times, with bounds that match with high probability for random instances.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary 3D systems are intended to let people interact with scenes through natural language. Evaluating them with a fixed set of object categories captures only part of that ability: people can refer to the same object using synonyms or more nuanced descriptions. OpenLex3D builds an evaluation benchmark around this linguistic variability.

The benchmark supplies new annotations for scenes from Replica, ScanNet++, and HM3D. These annotations introduce synonymous object categories and richer descriptions, providing thirteen times as many labels per scene as the original datasets. The additional labels expand how existing scene content can be described, making the evaluation less dependent on a narrow category vocabulary.

The authors evaluate existing methods using open-set 3D semantic segmentation and object retrieval tasks. Their experiments expose failure cases and provide insights into feature precision, segmentation, and downstream capabilities. The contribution is a more language-sensitive test of 3D representations: it examines how well systems connect varied descriptions to scene regions and objects, helping identify where current representations need improvement.
neurips-2025-openlex3d-a-tiered-benchmar.tldr: OpenLex3D tests 3D scene representations with synonyms and nuanced descriptions that go beyond fixed object-category labels.

paragraphs: In a multi-armed bandit problem, each available option produces uncertain rewards. This paper studies how to estimate the largest average reward using as few observations as possible. Given an error tolerance ε and confidence level 1−δ, the algorithm must return an estimate within ε of that largest mean with probability at least 1−δ.

The authors first derive an instance-dependent lower bound on the required number of samples. A difficulty is that the estimated value has infinitely many possible candidates, and the resulting bound involves non-convex optimization. This prevents a direct use of standard methods such as Track-and-Stop to establish optimality. The proposed solution combines two-phase sampling with a confidence-ellipsoid stopping rule.

The algorithm achieves the lower bound asymptotically, including matching constants in the leading term. This is a precise long-run sample-efficiency result, rather than an assertion of exact finite-sample optimality. The authors describe the method as simple and nearly free of hyperparameters, and report experiments supporting both the theoretical guarantees and its practical effectiveness.
neurips-2025-optimal-estimation-of-the-b.tldr: A two-phase bandit algorithm estimates the best mean reward with instance-dependent, asymptotically optimal sample complexity.

paragraphs: Learned image compressors trained on clean pictures can lose efficiency when their inputs contain degradations such as fog or rain. Training a separate compressor for every degradation is costly. This paper instead adapts the formation of compressed representations through learned prompts, aiming to align degraded inputs with the useful content represented in clean images.

The proposed IB-LRU scheme includes a probabilistic prompt generator that captures distributions of different degradations. Its prompts dynamically influence the encoder through gated modulation. An information bottleneck constrains prompt learning so that prompts focus on degradation characteristics while avoiding redundant image context. This gives the prompts a specific role: describing the corruption that the representation process should account for.

At the representation level, the method seeks compact information shared by degraded and clean images, connecting compression with restoration. The authors apply it to several leading learned-compression backbones and report effective results across different degradation scenarios. The contribution is a reusable adaptation scheme for handling varied degraded inputs, with experiments supporting its usefulness across the tested compressor architectures.
neurips-2025-prompt-guided-alignment-wit.tldr: Information-constrained prompts help learned image compressors handle degradations by aligning degraded and clean latent representations.

paragraphs: Protein design involves coupled choices about the amino-acid sequence, backbone structure, and side chains. Solving these separately can accumulate errors, motivating methods that generate them together. The authors identify a problem in existing all-atom approaches: side-chain information can reveal sequence information, allowing a model to take a shortcut instead of accurately learning the sequence distribution.

Their method introduces an information-flow strategy designed to eliminate this shortcut. It also develops a Bayesian flow formulation for backbone orientations. To do this, orientation modeling is recast as an equivalent generation problem on a hypersphere with antipodal symmetry. That symmetry makes opposite points equivalent within the representation, allowing the orientation problem to be expressed in the proposed form.

The resulting approach combines controlled information exchange with a Bayesian treatment of orientation generation. The authors report consistently strong performance on peptide and antibody design tasks. The key implication is that jointly modeling protein components requires attention to which information each component can access: richer all-atom information can otherwise undermine the distribution the model is meant to learn.
neurips-2025-rationalized-all-atom-prote.tldr: The method controls information flow to prevent sequence shortcuts and introduces Bayesian generation of backbone orientations for all-atom protein design.

paragraphs: Text-video retrieval learns representations that bring matching descriptions and videos together. The paper identifies two obstacles in contrastive training: a gap between the modalities creates tension in updates to anchor representations, and noisy hard negatives can distort their semantics. GARE addresses these problems by adding a learned correction specific to each text-video pair.

This increment redistributes gradients to relieve optimization tension and absorb noise. The authors derive it from a first-order Taylor expansion of the InfoNCE loss under a trust-region constraint, showing that it supports locally consistent descent directions. A lightweight neural module conditions corrections on the semantic gap and couples them across batches, allowing the adjustments to reflect shared structure rather than isolated pairs.

A variational information bottleneck with relaxed compression further regularizes the increments to improve stability and semantic consistency. Across four benchmarks, GARE consistently improves alignment accuracy and robustness. These results support modifying how mismatched representations are updated during training, with the theoretical descent claim applying locally under the stated trust-region formulation.
neurips-2025-rebalancing-contrastive-ali.tldr: GARE learns regularized pair-specific corrections that reduce alignment tension and noise in contrastive text-video retrieval.

paragraphs: Removing rain from nighttime images is complicated by the interaction between rain and illumination. A dataset that does not represent that interaction well can miss an important part of the task. The authors introduce HQ-NightRain, a benchmark designed to provide more realistic and visually harmonious nighttime rain examples than existing datasets.

They also develop CST-Net, a network built around a learnable color-space transformation. The motivation is that nighttime rain is more pronounced in the Y channel than in the RGB representation. A learned converter makes that representation useful for rain removal. Rather than treating the choice of color space as fixed, the method learns a transformation suited to the restoration task.

CST-Net additionally uses implicit illumination guidance so that learned features can account for lighting conditions and improve robustness in complex scenes. Experiments support both the value of the dataset and the effectiveness of the model. The work links better evaluation data with an architecture that explicitly responds to the coupled roles of color representation, illumination, and rain.
neurips-2025-rethinking-nighttime-image-.tldr: CST-Net learns a color representation and uses illumination guidance to remove nighttime rain, supported by a new realistic benchmark.

paragraphs: Neural representations describe how information appears in a network’s activations. Their geometry captures relationships among those representations, while dynamical analysis studies how a network changes over time. This paper connects the two perspectives by asking whether recurrent neural networks compute through ongoing changes in the geometry of represented task variables.

The authors hypothesize that recurrent networks dynamically warp these representations. To investigate, they develop a Riemannian geometric framework that derives the topology and geometry of a dynamical system’s representation manifold from the manifold of its inputs. In plain language, the framework links the structure of possible inputs to the shape and organization of the system’s internal representations.

Using this framework to characterize geometry over time, the authors find that dynamic warping is a fundamental feature of recurrent-network computation. The significance lies in treating representational shape as something that participates in computation as it evolves. This provides a mathematical bridge between descriptions of what a network represents and descriptions of how its time-dependent activity performs a task.
neurips-2025-rnns-perform-task-computati.tldr: A geometric framework connects recurrent-network dynamics with changing representation shapes, identifying dynamic warping as a fundamental computational feature.

paragraphs: Multi-camera 3D trackers must both detect objects and maintain their identities over time. Sharing parameters between these tasks can create optimization difficulties. The authors trace problems to self-attention that removes too many object-query candidates and keeps track queries overly focused on themselves. They find that removing self-attention barely affects regression predictions and tends to expose more candidate boxes.

SynCL builds on this analysis with a shared cross-attention decoder and task-specific hybrid matching. Track targets can match multiple object queries, allowing training to use promising candidates that self-attention and one-to-one matching might overlook. A dynamic filtering module adjusts candidate selection according to training status. Instance-aware contrastive learning further connects detection and tracking representations.

These changes form a plug-and-play training strategy without additional inference cost. SynCL consistently improves results across the evaluated benchmarks and reaches a reported state-of-the-art 58.9% AMOTA on nuScenes. The findings suggest that coordinating candidate matching and representation learning during training can improve the cooperation between detection and tracking within a shared model.
neurips-2025-syncl-a-synergistic-trainin.tldr: SynCL improves joint 3D detection and tracking through adaptive candidate matching and instance-aware contrastive training without extra inference cost.

paragraphs: Ultra-high-resolution image generation needs both suitable training images and a learning process that pays attention to fine detail. UltraHR-100K addresses the data requirement with 100,000 richly captioned images, each exceeding 3K resolution. The collection is curated for detail richness, content complexity, and aesthetic quality, providing varied material for text-to-image synthesis.

The authors also propose frequency-aware post-training for diffusion models. Detail-Oriented Timestep Sampling concentrates learning on denoising steps important for fine detail. Soft-Weighting Frequency Regularization uses the Discrete Fourier Transform to apply soft constraints to frequency components and encourage preservation of high-frequency information. The two mechanisms target when detail is learned and how it is retained.

Experiments on the authors’ UltraHR-eval4K benchmarks show significant improvements in fine-grained detail and overall image fidelity. The contribution therefore combines a curated data resource with training changes tailored to ultra-high resolution. Its findings support treating detail synthesis as a specific learning objective, alongside supplying images with enough visual information to learn that detail.
neurips-2025-ultrahr-100k-enhancing-uhr-.tldr: UltraHR-100K combines a curated high-resolution dataset with detail-focused diffusion post-training to improve ultra-high-resolution image synthesis.

paragraphs: Video diffusion models operate on compact tokens, but fixed temporal compression makes their computational cost grow with frame rate. VFRTok starts from a different proposed assumption: the upper bound on a video’s information capacity scales with its duration rather than its number of frames. This motivates representing videos without automatically adding proportional token capacity for every additional frame.

The transformer-based tokenizer supports variable frame rates by training its encoder and decoder with asymmetric frame rates. It also introduces Partial Rotary Position Embeddings to separate position modeling from content modeling. This helps group correlated patches into shared tokens and improves content awareness, producing a compact representation across space and time.

The authors report competitive reconstruction quality and state-of-the-art generation fidelity while using one-eighth as many tokens as existing tokenizers. These findings support the proposed representation’s efficiency in the evaluated settings. The duration-based information claim is the assumption guiding the design; the reported empirical result is that much smaller token representations can still support strong reconstruction and generation.
neurips-2025-vfrtok-variable-frame-rates.tldr: VFRTok supports variable video frame rates and reports strong generation quality using one-eighth as many tokens as existing tokenizers.
